title: More ways to say no: ne… plus, ne… personne, ne… que
summary: Say no longer, nobody, not a single, nowhere, neither… nor and only, in the present and the passé composé.
focus: The negative pairs beyond ne… pas, and where they go in the passé composé
content:
## More negative pairs

You know **ne… pas**, **ne… jamais** (never) and **ne… rien** (nothing). The new pairs wrap the verb the same way, **ne** (or **n'**) before it and the second word after it:

| pair | meaning | example |
|---|---|---|
| **ne… plus** | no longer, not any more | **Il ne travaille plus.** |
| **ne… personne** | nobody, not anybody | **Je ne connais personne.** |
| **ne… aucun / aucune** | not a single, no… at all | **Elle n'a aucune idée.** |
| **ne… nulle part** | nowhere, not anywhere | **On ne va nulle part.** |
| **ne… ni… ni…** | neither… nor… | **Je n'aime ni le thé ni le café.** |

As after **pas**, an article **un, une, du, des** becomes **de** after **plus**: **Il n'y a plus de pain.** **Plus jamais** means never again: **Je ne prends plus jamais ce bus.**

## Ne… que means only

**Ne… que** looks like a negation but it is not one: it means **only**. **Que** goes right before the thing it limits.

- **Je n'ai que dix euros.** I only have ten euros.
- **Il ne travaille que le matin.** He only works in the mornings.

Because nothing is denied, the article does **not** change: **Je ne bois que du thé** (I only drink tea), but **Je ne bois pas de thé** (I don't drink tea).

## Personne, rien and short answers

**Personne** and **rien** can be the subject. They come first, keep **ne**, take a singular verb, and never add **pas**:

- **Personne ne répond.** Nobody answers.
- **Rien ne marche.** Nothing works.

Alone, they answer a question: **Qui est là ? — Personne.** **Tu veux quoi ? — Rien.**

Two short answers:

- **non plus** agrees with a negative: **Je n'aime pas ça. — Moi non plus.** (Me neither.)
- **si** says yes to a negative question: **Tu ne viens pas ? — Si !** (Yes, I am!) **Oui** would sound odd here.

## Negation in the passé composé

The short words **pas, jamais, rien, plus** wrap **avoir** or **être**, so they sit before the participle:

- **Je n'ai rien vu.** I didn't see anything.
- **Il n'a jamais mangé d'escargots.** He has never eaten snails.

The longer ones, **personne, aucun, nulle part** and the **que** of **ne… que**, go after the participle:

- **Je n'ai vu personne.** I didn't see anybody.
- **Nous ne sommes allés nulle part.** We didn't go anywhere.
- **Elle n'a acheté qu'un livre.** She only bought one book.

quiz.prompt: Mon grand-père ne travaille ___ : il est à la retraite. (no longer)
quiz.explanation: Ne… plus says that something has stopped: il ne travaille plus. À la retraite = retired.
hints: Not pas: the work has stopped.

quiz.prompt: Which sentence means 'I didn't see anybody'?
quiz.explanation: Personne goes after the participle in the passé composé, and never with pas: je n'ai vu personne.
hints: Personne is one of the longer words.

quiz.prompt: Je n'ai ___ dix euros sur moi. (only)
quiz.explanation: Ne… que means only: je n'ai que dix euros. Que goes right before the amount.

quiz.prompt: 'Je n'ai que du pain' means 'I have no bread'.
quiz.explanation: False: ne… que means only, so it is 'I only have bread'. 'I have no bread' is je n'ai pas de pain; notice du stays after que.
hints: Ne… que is not a real negation.

quiz.prompt: Tu n'aimes pas le chocolat ? — ___, j'adore ça !
quiz.explanation: To say yes to a negative question, French uses si.
hints: The question is negative, the answer is yes.

quiz.prompt: ___ ne parle pendant le film : la salle est silencieuse. (nobody)
quiz.explanation: As the subject, personne comes first, keeps ne, takes a singular verb and no pas.

quiz.prompt: Léa n'a ___ ami dans sa nouvelle école. (not a single)
quiz.explanation: Ne… aucun agrees with the noun: ami is masculine, so aucun (une amie would give aucune).

quiz.prompt: How do you say 'I didn't eat anything' in the passé composé?
quiz.explanation: Rien is a short word: it wraps avoir with ne and sits before the participle.
hints: Rien goes where pas would go.

quiz.prompt: In 'Il n'y a plus de lait', de replaces du because of the negation.
quiz.explanation: True: after ne… plus, as after ne… pas, du / de la / des become de: il n'y a plus de lait.
hints: Like il n'y a pas de lait.

listening.meaning: I'm not going anywhere this weekend.

listening.text: Personne ne connaît la réponse à cette question.
listening.meaning: Nobody knows the answer to this question.
listening.note: New word: la réponse = the answer.

listening.text: Il n'y a plus de place dans le train ce soir.
listening.meaning: There's no more room on the train tonight.
listening.note: New word: la place = seat, room.

listening.text: Hier, je n'ai rien acheté et je n'ai vu personne au marché.
listening.meaning: Yesterday I didn't buy anything and I didn't see anybody at the market.
listening.note: Rien before the participle, personne after it.

guide.tip: Test ne… que by deleting it: 'Je n'ai que dix euros' still says you have ten euros. A real negation would take them away.

concept.title: Ne disappears in speech
concept.markdown: In relaxed spoken French the **ne** often drops out: **Je sais pas**, **Il y a personne**, **J'ai plus faim**. The second word carries the meaning. Write the **ne** and use it in careful speech; just recognise the short form when you hear it.

conversations.title: A quiet new village
conversations.scenario: Chloé has just moved to a small village. Her friend Samir phones to ask how it's going.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Alors, ta nouvelle vie à la campagne, ça va ?
lines.meaning: So, how's your new life in the countryside?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Bof. Je ne connais personne ici.
lines.meaning: Meh. I don't know anybody here.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Il y a un cinéma, une piscine ?
lines.meaning: Is there a cinema, a swimming pool?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Il n'y a ni cinéma ni piscine. Et la boulangerie n'ouvre que le matin.
lines.meaning: There's neither a cinema nor a pool. And the bakery only opens in the morning.

lines.speaker: a
lines.meaning: And do you go out in the evening?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Non, je ne vais nulle part. Il n'y a plus de bus après sept heures.
lines.meaning: No, I don't go anywhere. There are no more buses after seven.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Si, j'adore ma maison ! Elle est grande et calme.
lines.meaning: Yes, I love my house! It's big and quiet.
lines.note: si: yes to a negative question

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Tu as parlé avec tes voisins ?
lines.meaning: Have you talked to your neighbours?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Pas encore. Je n'ai vu personne dans la rue.
lines.meaning: Not yet. I haven't seen anybody in the street.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Je viens te voir samedi, d'accord ?
lines.meaning: I'm coming to see you on Saturday, OK?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Génial ! Je n'ai aucun projet samedi.
lines.meaning: Great! I have no plans at all on Saturday.

bites.title: No longer: ne… plus
bites.rule: Ne… plus wraps the verb like ne… pas and says something has stopped. Plus de + noun, and plus jamais = never again.
bites.example: Je ne mange plus de viande.
bites.example_meaning: I don't eat meat any more.

bites.title: Nobody, none, nowhere
bites.rule: Ne… personne (nobody), ne… aucun(e) (not a single), ne… nulle part (nowhere), ne… ni… ni… (neither… nor).

bites.title: Ne… que = only
bites.rule: Ne… que is not a negation: it means only, and the article stays: je ne bois que du thé.

bites.title: Si !
bites.rule: Say yes to a negative question with si. Personne ne… and rien ne… can start a sentence, with no pas.
bites.example_meaning: Aren't you coming? — Yes, I am!

sorts.title: What does it mean?

items.text: Je ne lis que le soir.
Je ne voyage nulle part cet été.

sorts.why: Plus = no longer, personne = nobody, que = only, nulle part = nowhere.

sorts.title: Before or after the participle?
sorts.why: The short words wrap avoir: je n'ai rien vu. Personne, aucun and nulle part come after the participle: je n'ai vu personne.

spots.sentence: Il n'y a plus du pain.
spots.why: After ne… plus, du becomes de.

spots.sentence: Tu ne viens pas ? — Oui, j'arrive !
spots.why: Yes to a negative question is si.

spots.sentence: Je n'aime ni le thé ou le café.

realm.content:
## Le donjon vide à Eldmark

The dungeon is empty: **il n'y a personne**, **il n'y a plus de butin**, **aucun coffre**. Borin **ne trouve son épée nulle part** and Nym **n'a que deux potions**. **Personne ne** parle. « Tu n'as pas peur ? — **Si** ! » Same pairs, same places as in the lesson.

vocabulary.example_meaning: There are no potions left in my bag.

sorts.title: Negation or only?

items.text: Nous ne buvons que de l'eau.

sorts.why: Ne… que only limits: you still have the thing. Plus, personne and nulle part really deny.

quiz.prompt: Dans le donjon vide, Borin ne voit ___. (nobody)
quiz.explanation: Ne… personne = nobody: Borin ne voit personne.

quiz.prompt: Nym the elf only has one arrow left. Which sentence says so?
quiz.explanation: Ne… que = only; before une, que becomes qu'.

meadowbrook.content:
## Les chenilles à Meadowbrook

Caterpillars visited your vegetable patch: **il n'y a plus de fraises**, **je n'ai que trois citrouilles**, and **je ne trouve mes poules nulle part**. **Personne ne** vend de graines today. « Tu n'es pas triste ? — **Si**, un peu. » Next season, **plus jamais** de chenilles!

vocabulary.example_meaning: There are no strawberries left in the vegetable patch.

Tu n'aimes pas les champignons ? — Oui, j'adore !
spots.why: Yes to a negative question is si.

sorts.title: Before or after the participle?
sorts.why: Rien, jamais and pas wrap avoir / être; personne, nulle part and aucun come after the participle.

quiz.prompt: Les chenilles ont tout mangé : il n'y a ___ de fraises dans le potager. (no more)
quiz.explanation: Ne… plus says something has stopped or run out: il n'y a plus de fraises.

quiz.prompt: 'Je n'ai que trois citrouilles' means Nora has no pumpkins at all.
quiz.explanation: False: ne… que = only. Nora has three pumpkins, and only three.
hints: Ne… que is not a real negation.

rustwake.content:
## La ferraille à Rustwake

A bad day in the scrap village: **il n'y a plus d'eau filtrée**, Marta **n'a que dix écrous**, **personne ne** répond à la radio, and Léo **n'a rien trouvé** in the bins. « Tu n'as pas soif ? — **Si** ! » In the desert as in Paris, the same negative pairs.

sorts.why: Plus = no longer, personne = nobody, que = only.

quiz.prompt: Pendant la tempête de cendres, ___ ne sort du village. (nobody)

quiz.prompt: Léo searched the bins and found nothing. Which sentence is right?
quiz.explanation: Rien wraps avoir and sits before the participle: n'a rien trouvé.
hints: Rien goes where pas would go.
